tr.text: Now the meditation (on the Udgitha) with reference to the gods is described. One should meditate on him who gives heat (i.e. the sun) as Udgitha. Verily, he who knows the sun as being endowed with these qualities, becomes the dispeller of darkness and (the consequent) fear.

alt.text: Breath & the Sun are one & alike — for the one is heat & the other is heat, and they call Breath the mover and the Sun too they call the mover & they call him also the mover that returneth upon his paths — therefore ye shall worship both the one & the other as Udgitha.

tr.text: This Prana in the mouth and that sun are the same. This is warm and that is warm. People call this as Svara (that is going) and that as Svara and Pratyasvara (that is going and coming). Therefore one should meditate on this Prana and that sun as Udgitha.

sa: अथ यः प्राणापानयोः संधिः स व्यानः ।

alt.text: Thereafter verily ye shall worship Vyana the middle breath as Udgitha. For when one breathes forth it is Prana, the Main Breath, & when one breathes down it is Apana, the lower breath. Now this which is the joint & linking of the main breath & the lower breath, is Vyana — & Vyana, it is Speech. Therefore ’tis when one neither breatheth forth nor breatheth down that one giveth utterance to Speech.

tr.text: Now, verily one should meditate on Vyana as Udgitha. That which one breathes out is Prana and that which one breathes in is Apana. The junction of Prana and Apana is Vyana. That which is Vyana, even that is speech. Therefore, one utters speech while one neither breathes out nor breathes in.

alt.text: But Speech is the Rik — therefore ’tis when one neither breatheth out nor breatheth in that one uttereth the Rik. And Rik it is Sama — therefore ’tis when one neither breatheth out nor breatheth in that one chanteth the Sama. But Sama it is Udgitha — therefore ’tis when one neither breatheth out nor breatheth in that one singeth Udgitha.

tr.text: That which is speech, even that is Rik. Therefore while one neither breathes out nor breathes in, one pronounces the Rik. That which is Rik, even that is Saman. Therefore, while one neither breathes out nor breathes in, one sings the Saman. That which is Saman, even that is Udgitha. Therefore, while one neither breathes out nor breathes in, one sings the Udgitha.

sa: अतो यान्य् अन्यानि वीर्यवन्ति कर्माणि यथाग्नेर् मन्थनम् आजेः सरणं दृढस्य धनुष आयमनम् अप्राणन्न् अनपानंस् तानि करोति ।

alt.text: Hence whatsoever actions there be that are of might & forcefulness as smiting out fire from the tinder or leaping a great barrier or bending a stark & mighty bow, it is when one neither breatheth out nor breatheth in that one doeth these. And for this cause ye shall worship the middle breath as Udgitha.

tr.text: Therefore whatever other actions require strength, such as the kindling of fire by friction, running a race towards a goal, the bending of a strong bow, are all performed, while one neither breathes out nor breathes in. For this reason one should meditate on Vyana as Udgitha.

alt.text: Thereafter verily ye shall worship the syllables of the Udgitha saying Udgitha & Prana is the first syllable, because one riseth up with the main breath & Speech is the second syllable, because they call Speech that which goeth forth & food is the third syllable, because in food all this Universe is established.

tr.text: Now, one should meditate on the syllables of ‘Udgitha’ – namely, the syllables ‘ut’, ‘gi’ and ‘tha’. Prana is ‘ut’, because through Prana one arises (ut-tisthati). Speech is ‘gi’, because speech is called word (girah). Food is ‘tha’, because upon food all this is established (sthitam).

sa: दुग्धे ऽस्मै वाग् दोहं यो वाचो दोहः ।
य एतान्य् एवं विद्वान् उद्गीथाक्षराण्य् उपास्त उद्-गी-थ इति ॥
iast: dugdhe ’smai vāg dohaṃ yo vāco dohaḥ ।
ya etāny evaṃ vidvān udgīthākṣarāṇy upāsta ud-gī-tha iti ॥

alt.text: Heaven is the first syllable, the middle air is the second syllable, earth is the third syllable. The Sun is the first syllable, Air is the second syllable, Fire is the third syllable. The Samaveda is the first syllable, Yajurveda is the second syllable, Rigveda is the third syllable. To him Speech is a cow that yieldeth sweet milk — & what is this milking of Speech? — even that he becometh rich in food & the eater of food who knoweth these & worshippeth the syllables of Udgitha saying lo even this is Udgitha.

tr.text: Heaven is ut, the sky is gi, the earth is tha. The sun is ut, the air gi, the fire, tha. The Sama-Veda is ut, the Yajur-Veda gi, the Rig-Veda tha. For him, speech yields the milk which is the benefit of speech. And he becomes rich in food; and an eater of food, who knows thus and meditates on the syllables of ‘Udgitha’, namely, ut, gi and tha.

tr.text: One should meditate on the syllable Om, the Udgitha, for one sings the Udgitha beginning with Om. Of this the explanation follows.

sa: देवा वै मृत्योर् बिभ्यतस् त्रयीं विद्यां प्राविशन् ।
यद् एभिर् अच्छादयंस् तच् छन्दसां छन्दस्त्वम् ॥

yad ebhir acchādayaṃs tac chandasāṃ chandastvam ॥

tr.text: Verily, the gods, being afraid of death, took refuge in the three Vedas. They covered themselves with the metrical hymns. Because they covered themselves with these, the metrical hymns are called Chandas.

ते नु वित्त्वोर्ध्वा ऋचः साम्नो यजुषः स्वरम् एव प्राविशन् ॥

tr.text: Just as a fisherman would see a fish in water, so did Death observe the gods in the (rites connected with) Rik, Saman and Yajus. They, too, knowing this, arose from the Rik, Saman and Yajus, and entered the Svara (the syllable Om).

tr.text: Verily, when one learns the Rik, he loudly pronounces ‘Om’. It is the same with Saman and with Yajus. This syllable Om is indeed Svara; it again is immortality and fearlessness. Having entered into Svara (i.e. having meditated) the gods became immortal and fearless.

sa: स य एतद् एवं विद्वान् अक्षरं प्रणौत्य् एतद् एवाक्षरं स्वरम् अमृतम् अभयं प्रविशति ।
तत् प्रविश्य यद् अमृता देवास् तद् अमृतो भवति ॥
iast: sa ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaraṃ praṇauty etad evākṣaraṃ svaram amṛtam abhayaṃ praviśati ।
tat praviśya yad amṛtā devās tad amṛto bhavati ॥

tr.text: He who worships this syllable knowing it thus, enters this syllable, the Svara, which is immortality and fearlessness. And having entered it, he becomes immortal by that nectar, by which the gods became immortal.

tr.text: Now, this person who is seen within the eye – he indeed is Rik, he is Saman, he is Uktha, he is Yajus, he is the Vedas. words: to sing to; to address or praise in singing; to sing in order to obtain anything

tr.text: Similarly, through this person in the eye, one gets the worlds that are extended below this person, and also the desired objects of men. For this reason, the Udgatir priest who knows thus should ask (the sacrificer): ‘What desire shall I obtain for you by singing the Saman ?’ For he alone becomes capable of obtaining desires by singing , who knowing thus sings the Saman – yea, sings the Saman.

sa: त्रयो होद्गीथे कुशला बभूवुः शिलकः शालावत्यश् चैकितायनो दाल्भ्यः प्रवाहणो जैवलिर् इति ।
ते होचुर् उद्गीथे वै कुशलाः स्मो हन्तोद्गीथे कथां वदाम इति ॥
iast: trayo hodgīthe kuśalā babhūvuḥ śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyano dālbhyaḥ pravāhaṇo jaivalir iti ।
te hocur udgīthe vai kuśalāḥ smo hantodgīthe kathāṃ vadāma iti ॥
words: a king of the Śālāvatas; patr. from śalāvat
patr. of Keśin; name of Vaka; name of Caikitāyana

tr.text: In ancient times there were three proficient in Udgitha: Silaka the son of Salavat, Caikitayana of the Dalbhya family and Pravahana the son of Jivala. They said, ‘We are proficient in Udgitha. If you agree, let us enter on a discussion of Udgitha’.

words: to sit down together or near; to sit down on; to lie down upon (acc.)

tr.text: ‘Let it be so’, saying this they sat down. Then Pravahana Jaivali said, ‘You two, revered sirs, speak first; and I shall listen to the words of two Brahmanas conversing’.

sa: स ह शिलकः शालावत्यश् चैकितायनं दाल्भ्यम् उवाच हन्त त्वा पृच्छानीति ।
iast: sa ha śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyanaṃ dālbhyam uvāca hanta tvā pṛcchānīti ।
words: a king of the Śālāvatas; patr. from śalāvat
patr. of Keśin; name of Vaka; name of Caikitāyana

tr.text: Then Silaka Salavatya said to Caikitayana Dalbhya, ‘If you permit, I shall question you’. ‘Question’, said he.

(Silaka asked), ‘What is the essence of Saman ?’ ‘The tune’, said (Dalbhya). ‘What is the essence of the tune ?’ ‘Prana’, said (Dalbhya). ‘What is the essence of Prana ?’ ‘Food’, said (Dalbhya). ‘What is the essence of food ?’ ‘Water’, said (Dalbhya).

sa: न स्वर्गं लोकम् अतिनयेद् इति होवाच ।
iast: na svargaṃ lokam atinayed iti hovāca ।
words: to lead over or beyond; to help a person over anything; to allow to pass away
hymning or praising in chorus; simultaneous or common praise

tr.text: ‘What is the essence of water ?’ ‘That (heavenly world)’, said (Dalbhya). ‘What is the essence of the world ?’ ‘One cannot carry (the Saman) beyond the heavenly world’, said Dalbhya; ‘we locate the Saman in the world of heaven, for Saman is praised as heaven’.

sa: तं ह शिलकः शालावत्यश् चैकितायनं दाल्भ्यम् उवाचाप्रतिष्ठितं वै किल ते दाल्भ्य साम ।
यस् त्व् एतर्हि ब्रूयान् मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति मूर्धा ते विपतेद् इति ॥
iast: taṃ ha śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyanaṃ dālbhyam uvācāpratiṣṭhitaṃ vai kila te dālbhya sāma ।
yas tv etarhi brūyān mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mūrdhā te vipated iti ॥
words: a king of the Śālāvatas; patr. from śalāvat
patr. of Keśin; name of Vaka; name of Caikitāyana
patr. of Keśin; name of Vaka; name of Caikitāyana

tr.text: Then Silaka Salavatya said to Caikitayana Dalbhya: ‘O Dalbhya, your Saman is not indeed established. If someone one were to say, "Your head shall fall down", surely your head would fall down’.

sa: न प्रतिष्ठां लोकम् अतिनयेद् इति होवाच ।
iast: na pratiṣṭhāṃ lokam atinayed iti hovāca ।
words: to lead over or beyond; to help a person over anything; to allow to pass away
hymning or praising in chorus; simultaneous or common praise

tr.text: (Dalbhya) ‘Will you permit me, sir, to learn this of you ?’ ‘Learn’, said (Silaka). ‘What is the essence of that (heavenly) world ?’ ‘This earth’, said (Silaka), ‘What is the essence of this earth ?’ ‘One cannot carry the Saman beyond this world as its support’, said Silaka; ‘we locate the Saman in this world as its support, for Saman is extolled as the earth’.

sa: अन्तवद् वै किल ते शालावत्य साम ।
यस् त्व् एतर्हि ब्रूयान् मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति मूर्धा ते विपतेद् इति ।
iast: antavad vai kila te śālāvatya sāma ।
yas tv etarhi brūyān mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mūrdhā te vipated iti ।
words: a king of the Śālāvatas; patr. from śalāvat

tr.text: Pravahana Jaivali said to him, ‘O Salavatya, your Sama, really, has a further end. If someone now were to say, "Your head shall fall down", surely your head would fall down. (Salavatya) ‘Will you permit me, sir, to learn (this of you ?) ‘Learn’, said (Jaivali).

sa: सर्वाणि ह वा इमानि भूतान्य् आकाशाद् एव समुत्पद्यन्ते ।
iast: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāny ākāśād eva samutpadyante ।
words: to spring up together; to be brought forth or born of; to arise

tr.text: (Salavatya) ‘What is the essence of this world ?’ ‘Akasa’ said (Pravahana); ‘All these beings arise from Akasa alone and are finally dissolved into Akasa; because Akasa alone is greater than all these and Akasa is the support at all times.’

sa: परोवरीयो हास्य भवति परोवरीयसो ह लोकाञ् जयति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् परोवरीयांसम् उद्गीथम् उपास्ते ॥
iast: parovarīyo hāsya bhavati parovarīyaso ha lokāñ jayati ya etad evaṃ vidvān parovarīyāṃsam udgītham upāste ॥

tr.text: It is this Udgitha which is progressively higher and better. This again is endless. He who, knowing thus, meditates upon the progressively higher and better Udgitha, obtains progressively higher and better lives and wins progressively higher and better worlds.

sa: यावत् त एनं प्रजायाम् उद्गीथं वेदिष्यन्ते परोवरीयो हैभ्यस् तावद् अस्मिंल् लोके जीवनं भविष्यति ॥
iast: yāvat ta enaṃ prajāyām udgīthaṃ vediṣyante parovarīyo haibhyas tāvad asmiṃl loke jīvanaṃ bhaviṣyati ॥
words: life; manner of living; living by (instr. or in comp.)

tr.text: Atidhanvan, the son of Sunaka, having taught this to Udarasandilya, said, ‘As long as among your descendants, this knowledge of the Udgitha continues, so long their life in this world will be progressively higher and better than ordinary lives.’

sa: स य एतम् एव विद्वान् उपास्ते परोवरीय एव हास्यामुष्मिंल् लोके जीवनं भवति तथामुष्मिंल् लोके लोक इति लोके लोक इति ॥
iast: sa ya etam eva vidvān upāste parovarīya eva hāsyāmuṣmiṃl loke jīvanaṃ bhavati tathāmuṣmiṃl loke loka iti loke loka iti ॥
words: life; manner of living; living by (instr. or in comp.)

tr.text: ‘And in that other world also their state will be similar’. He who knows and meditates thus – his life in this world surely becomes progressively higher and better, and so also his state in that other world – yea, in that other world.

sa: मटचीहतेषु कुरुष्व् आटिक्या सह जाययोषस्तिर् ह चाक्रायण इभ्यग्रामे प्रद्राणक उवास ॥
iast: maṭacīhateṣu kuruṣv āṭikyā saha jāyayoṣastir ha cākrāyaṇa ibhyagrāme pradrāṇaka uvāsa ॥
words: name of the wife of Ushasti
belonging to one's servants or attendants
sorely distressed; very needy or poor

tr.text: When the crops in the Kuru country had been destroyed by hailstorms, there lived Usasti, the son of Cakra with his young wife in a deplorable condition in the village of elephant-drivers.

sa: नेतो ऽन्ये विद्यन्ते यच् च ये म इम उपनिहिता इति ॥
iast: neto ’nye vidyante yac ca ye ma ima upanihitā iti ॥

sour gruel; an inferior kind of grain; half-ripe barley
to chew; to bite; to eat
to put or place down near to; to put or place before; to place down

tr.text: He begged food of an elephant-driver, while he was eating beans of an inferior quality. The driver said to him, ‘There is no other food than what is set before me’.

sa: उच्छिष्टं वै मे पीतं स्याद् इति होवाच ॥
iast: ucchiṣṭaṃ vai me pītaṃ syād iti hovāca ॥
words: a fluid vehicle in medicine; drink taken with or after medicine; drink after eating

tr.text: ‘Give me some of them’, said Usasti. The driver gave them to him and said, ‘Here is drink at hand, if you please 1’ ‘Then I shall be drinking what is defiled’, said Usasti.

sa: न स्विद् एते ऽप्य् उच्छिष्टा इति ।
न वा अजीविष्यम् इमान् अखादन्न् इति होवाच ।
iast: na vā ajīviṣyam imān akhādann iti hovāca ।
words: to leave as a remainder; to be impure; to be impure with the remnants of food
to chew; to bite; to eat
(only at the beginning or end of a compound) water

tr.text: ‘Are not these beans also defiled ?’ ‘Unless I ate them, I would surely not have survived’, said Usasti, ‘but drinking is at my option’.

words: to chew; to bite; to eat

tr.text: Usasti, after he had eaten, brought the remainder to his wife. She had already obtained her food by alms; so after receiving it she kept it by.

words: the office or business of a Ṛtvij or sacrificing priest

tr.text: Next morning while leaving the bed he said, ‘Alas, if I could get a little of food, I could earn a little wealth. There a king is going to institute a sacrifice; he would appoint me to all the priestly offices’.

sa: हन्त पत इम एव कुल्माषा इति ।
iast: hanta pata ima eva kulmāṣā iti ।
words: sour gruel; an inferior kind of grain; half-ripe barley
to chew; to bite; to eat

tr.text: His wife said to him, ‘Well, lord, here are the beans (given by you).’ Having eaten them he went off to that sacrifice which was being performed.

words: the place where a particular Stotra is sung; praising-ground; place for chanting
to praise; to celebrate; to extol
name of the assistant of the Udgātṛ (who chants the Prastāva)

tr.text: Seeing the singing priests seated there, he sat down near the singers in the place for singing the Stotras. And then he addressed the Prastotir priest.

sa: प्रस्तोतर् या देवता प्रस्तावम् अन्वायत्ता तां चेद् अविद्वान् प्रस्तोष्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति ॥
iast: prastotar yā devatā prastāvam anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān prastoṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti ॥
words: name of the assistant of the Udgātṛ (who chants the Prastāva)
to praise before (anything else) or aloud; to sing; to chant (in general)

tr.text: ‘O Prastotir, if you sing the Prastava without knowing the deity that belongs to the Prastava, your head will fall down’.

sa: उद्गातर् या देवतोद्गीथम् अन्वायत्ता तां चेद् अविद्वान् उद्गास्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति ॥
iast: udgātar yā devatodgītham anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān udgāsyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti ॥

tr.text: In the same manner he addressed the Udgatir priest, O Udgatir, if you sing the Udgitha without knowing the deity that belongs to the Udgitha, your head will fall down’.

sa: प्रतिहर्तर् या देवता प्रतिहारम् अन्वायत्ता तां चेद् अविद्वान् प्रतिहरिष्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति ।
ते ह समारतास् तूष्णीम् आसां चक्रिरे ॥
iast: pratihartar yā devatā pratihāram anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān pratihariṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti ।
te ha samāratās tūṣṇīm āsāṃ cakrire ॥

one who draws back or absorbs; a destroyer; one who keeps or wards off
to throw back; to strike or pound; to keep shut

tr.text: In the same manner he addressed the Pratihartir priest, ‘O Pratihartir, if you sing the Pratihara without knowing the deity that belongs to the Pratihara, your head will fall down’. Then they all sat down silently suspending their duties.
Then the principal of the sacrifice said to him, I should like to know you, revered sir, ‘I am Chakrayana Usasti’, said he.

sa: भगवन्तं वा अहम् एभिः सर्वैर् आर्त्विज्यैः पर्यैषिषम् ।
iast: bhagavantaṃ vā aham ebhiḥ sarvair ārtvijyaiḥ paryaiṣiṣam ।
words: the office or business of a Ṛtvij or sacrificing priest
the not finding; the not possessing; poverty

tr.text: He said, ‘I searched for you, revered sir, for all these priestly offices, but not finding you, sir, I have chosen others.’

sa: भगवांस् त्व् एव मे सर्वैर् आर्त्विज्यैर् इति ।
अथ तर्ह्य् एत एव समतिसृष्टाः स्तुवताम् ।
यावत् त्व् एभ्यो धनं दद्यास् तावन् मम दद्या इति ।
iast: bhagavāṃs tv eva me sarvair ārtvijyair iti ।
atha tarhy eta eva samatisṛṣṭāḥ stuvatām ।
yāvat tv ebhyo dhanaṃ dadyās tāvan mama dadyā iti ।
words: the office or business of a Ṛtvij or sacrificing priest
to praise; to celebrate; to extol

tr.text: ‘Revered sir, you yourself take up all the priestly offices for me’. ‘Be it so; then, let these same priests sing the hymns, being permitted by me. But you should give me as much wealth as you give them.’ ‘Very well’, said the sacrificer.

sa: प्रस्तोतर् या देवता प्रस्तावम् अन्वायत्ता तां चेद् अविद्वान् प्रस्तोष्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति मा भगवान् अवोचत् ।
iast: prastotar yā devatā prastāvam anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān prastoṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mā bhagavān avocat ।
words: name of the assistant of the Udgātṛ (who chants the Prastāva)
name of the assistant of the Udgātṛ (who chants the Prastāva)

tr.text: Then the Prastotir priest approached him and said, ‘Revered sir, you said to me: ‘O Prastotir, if you sing the Prastava without knowing the deity that belongs to the Prastava, your head will fall down". Which is that deity ?’

sa: सर्वाणि ह वा इमानि भूतानि प्राणम् एवाभिसंविशन्ति ।
तां चेद् अविद्वान् प्रास्तोष्यो मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यत् तथोक्तस्य मयेति ॥
iast: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāni prāṇam evābhisaṃviśanti ।
tāṃ ced avidvān prāstoṣyo mūrdhā te vipatiṣyat tathoktasya mayeti ॥
words: to praise before (anything else) or aloud; to sing; to chant (in general)

tr.text: ‘Prana’, said Usasti, ‘all these movable and immovable beings merge in Prana (during dissolution) and rise out of Prana (during creation). This is the deity that belongs to the Prastava. If you sang the Prastava without knowing him, after your having been warned thus by me, your head would have fallen down.’

sa: उद्गातर् या देवतोद्गीथम् अन्वायत्ता तां चेद् अविद्वान् उद्गास्यसि मूर्धा ते विपतिष्यतीति मा भगवान् अवोचत् ।

tr.text: Then the Udgatir priest approached him and said, ‘Revered sir, you said to me: ‘O Udgatir, if you sing the Udgitha without knowing the deity that belongs to the Udgitha, your head will fall down". Which is that deity ?’

sa: सर्वाणि ह वा इमानि भूतान्य् आदित्यम् उच्चैः सन्तं गायन्ति ।
तां चेद् अविद्वान् उदगास्यो मूर्धा ते व्यपतिष्यत् तथोक्तस्य मयेति ॥

tāṃ ced avidvān udagāsyo mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyat tathoktasya mayeti ॥

tr.text: ‘The sun’, said Usasti, ‘all these movable and immovable sing the praise of the sun when he has come up. This is the deity that belongs to the Udgitha. If you sang the Udgitha without knowing him, after your having been warned thus by me, your head would have fallen down.’

तां चेद् अविद्वान् प्रत्यहरिष्यो मूर्धा ते व्यपतिष्यत् तथोक्तस्य मयेति तथोक्तस्य मयेति ॥

tr.text: ‘Food’, said Usasti, ‘all these movable and immovable beings live by partaking of food only. This is the deity that belongs to the Pratihara. If you sang the Pratihara without knowing him, after your having been warned thus by me, your head would have fallen down.’

tr.text: Therefore next begins the Udgitha seen by the dogs. Once Dalbhya Baka, called also Maitreya Glava, went out (of the village) for the study of the Vedas.
Before him a white dog appeared and other dogs gathered around it and said, ‘Revered sir, please obtain food for us by singing; we are hungry.’

sa: तद् ध बको दाल्भ्यो ग्लावो वा मैत्रेयः प्रतिपालयां चकार ॥

tr.text: The white dog said to them, ‘Come to me over here tomorrow morning.’ (The sage named) Dalbhya Baka and Maitreya Glava kept watch there for them.

sa: ते ह यथैवेदं बहिष्पवमानेन स्तोष्यमाणाः संरब्धाः सर्पन्तीत्य् एवम् आससृपुः ।
iast: te ha yathaivedaṃ bahiṣpavamānena stoṣyamāṇāḥ saṃrabdhāḥ sarpantīty evam āsasṛpuḥ ।

tr.text: Just as those who recite the Stotras singing the Bahispavamana hymn move along clasping one another’s hand, even so did the dogs move along. Then they sat down and began to pronounce ‘him’.

tr.text: ‘Om, let us eat ! Om, let us drink ! Om, may the (sun who is) god, Varuna, Prajapati and Savitir bring us food here. O Lord of food, bring food here, yea bring it, Om !’
Verily, this world is the syllable ‘hau’ (which is a Stobha), the air is the syllable ‘hai’, the moon is the syllable ‘atha’, the self is the syllable ‘iha’ and the fire is the syllable ‘I’.

words: invocation; calling; name of a Sāman
